outcome: Help educators give each learner timely, curriculum-aligned support without removing teacher judgement.
overview: Teachers rarely have time to interpret fragmented learning signals and build differentiated support for every learner. This solution combines approved curriculum, learning activity, assessment evidence and educator-defined rules to identify knowledge gaps and recommend suitable explanations, practice and interventions in Arabic and English. Teachers approve every plan and can inspect why each recommendation was made; nothing reaches a learner without educator sign-off. An 8–12-week proof of value runs on a historical cohort before any live pilot, targeting faster gap identification, reduced planning effort and stronger progress visibility, with bias monitoring across learner groups and a full record of every intervention for leaders, families and inspectors.

benefits.text: Identify learning gaps a target 30% faster than the current manual review cycle
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against the institution’s own baseline term
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate in a controlled pilot term — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce teacher planning effort for differentiated support by a target 20%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on curriculum-map quality and educator adoption of the review workflow

benefits.text: Give leaders and families consistent, explainable intervention records for every supported learner
benefits.source: Reference design — every recommendation carries an explanation and an audit entry
benefits.limits: Record completeness depends on educators logging outcomes in the workflow

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); learner data never leaves the institution’s tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No usable assessment data or curriculum map in the learning platform
notFor.why: Gap identification needs curriculum-aligned assessment evidence to reason over; without it recommendations cannot be grounded

notFor.situation: The institution wants fully automated tutoring without educator review
notFor.why: The design keeps teachers approving every plan — autonomous high-impact decisions about learners are out of scope by policy

notFor.situation: No consent and privacy basis for using learner data in analytics
notFor.why: Minor and student data requires an approved lawful basis and age-appropriate consent before any modelling

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns curriculum, intervention policy and privacy approval · Duration: 8–12 weeks PoV; 16–24 weeks to production deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, learning-analytics data scientist, integration engineer; customer academic owner, LMS/SIS administrator, data-protection officer, educator champions · Support model: Business-hours support with term-time escalation cover; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Data and curriculum validation
3) Model and workflow build
4) Educator review and co-design
5) Accessibility and security testing
6) Controlled pilot and benefit review
